thread:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired: PD-7342 — service=autoscaler-queue-monitor — severity=critical. Symptoms: queue depth > 100k, avg processing latency 12s+, error spike. Link: https://pagerduty.example/PD-7342

maria: ack — I'm taking lead. tagging infra: @kevin please grab autoscaler logs & HPA events, dani can you check recent config changes?

kevin: looking now. dashboards show replicas stuck at 8 for last 6m while queue grew. HPA events show repeated errors: 'unable to compute metrics: resource metrics not available'. grabbing controller logs.

kevin: logs snippet:
```
I050 14:02:10.123 HPA controller: failed to get cpu metrics for deployment/autoscale-workers: no metrics returned
I050 14:02:11.234 HPA controller: calculated desired replicas=62 based on queue length
I050 14:02:11.235 HPA controller: scaling suppressed: maxReplicas=20
```

dani: fwiw earlier deploy (09:12) changed the autoscaler policy — someone reduced maxReplicas to 20 for cost testing. That change landed in prod. cc @ops-runner.

luca: oof. manual scale now to buy time. running:
```bash
kubectl -n inference scale deployment/autoscale-workers --replicas=60
```

ops-runner: executed manual scale -> replicas=60. Watching queue.

maria: PagerDuty PD-7342 acknowledged by maria (incident-bot). Escalation paused.

kevin: after scale, worker utilization ~60% and pod startup lag ~20s. queue depth dropping from 102k -> 28k in 6m. latency down from 12s to ~4s p95.

maria: customer impact update: initial spike caused ~3% of requests to time out (gateway 502/504) across EU region for ~12m window. No data loss, just retries. Notifying support for incident banner?

dani: creating rollback PR to revert maxReplicas=20 change, adding test to prevent runtime-policy changes without a canary. PR: https://git.example/r/autoscale/pull/458

kevin: also adding a guard alert — a config-drift monitor that flags policy changes to autoscaler config before they reach prod. Filed INF-1234 (follow-up).

luca: removing the temporary cap on HPA now (patching HPA):
```bash
kubectl -n inference patch hpa autoscale-workers -p '{"spec":{"maxReplicas":200}}'
```

ops-runner: patched, confirmed HPA target respected. scaling events resuming automatically. queue trending down, estimated clear time ~8m.

maria: PD: escalating to on-call rotation if any regressions. For now keeping PD open until follow-ups are triaged.

pagerduty-bot: PD-7342 escalation: notified on-call rotation (ops-runner).

kevin: root cause summary for handoff: manual change earlier today set maxReplicas too low which capped HPA. Also metrics hiccup delayed HPA decision for a couple minutes. Mitigation: manual scale + revert config + patch HPA + config-drift alert.

maria: handing off to day SRE team for post-incident work. ops-runner please own INF-1234 and the rollback PR until merged. I'll update incident timeline and write up draft.

ops-runner: got it, taking ownership. Will follow up with cadence and link postmortem.

maria: closing notes: incident resolved (queue drained, autoscaler functioning) at 2026-03-14T15:13:55Z. Impact: transient increased latency and ~3% timeouts for EU customers, ~12m. Next steps: merge PR, add config-drift alert, add pre-deploy policy check.

maria: resolving PD after follow-ups filed. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

kevin: good run — log the deploy change in change log so this doesn't sneak past review again.

luca: will add a readonly dashboard to show current maxReplicas vs desired so we can catch caps earlier.

incident-bot: PD-7342 marked resolved by maria.

maria: closing thread. follow-ups: INF-1234 (config-drift alert), PR 458 (rollback), DOC-77 (runbook update).
